html:
The killing of ethnic Chinese in Batavia, now Jakarta, by soldiers of the Dutch East India Company and other residents of the city in October 1740. Historians estimate at least 10,000 died.

Batavia had a large Chinese community of traders, craftsmen and workers on the sugar estates around the city. When sugar prices fell in the 1730s, many lost their jobs, and the Company tried to send the jobless away to Ceylon. A rumour spread that the deportees were being thrown overboard at sea. Chinese bands outside the walls rose up and attacked. Inside the city, officials feared the Chinese were plotting, and from 9 October soldiers and townspeople went house to house killing Chinese residents. Governor General Adriaan Valckenier was later arrested over the affair.

The survivors were made to live outside the walls in a district that became Glodok, still Jakarta's Chinatown. Chinese fighters who escaped joined Javanese forces in a war against the Company that spread across central Java until 1743. The massacre is remembered as a turning point for the Chinese of Indonesia. See also the founding of Batavia.
sum: The killing of ethnic Chinese in Batavia, now Jakarta, by soldiers of the Dutch East India Company and other residents of the city in October 1740. Historians estimate at least 10,000 died.
